harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1 (Alpine Linux 3.23, busybox crond/crontab via bbsuid), restricted cron scheduling to root and opsadmin only. Since busybox crontab has no cron.allow/cron.deny support, implemented access control via a wrapper: moved the real crontab binary (symlink to /bin/bbsuid) into a root:cron-owned directory /usr/libexec/cron-real (mode 0710, blocking traversal by non-root/non-cron-group users), and replaced /usr/bin/crontab with a shell wrapper that checks the caller's username against an allowlist (root, opsadmin) before exec'ing the real binary. Created the opsadmin user with a locally generated random password, added opsadmin to the cron group, enabled and started the crond service (rc-update add crond default), and verified end-to-end: root and opsadmin can list/install/remove crontabs, the existing 'alpine' user is denied both via the wrapper and via direct-path bypass attempts. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured pre-restart boot_id and service health, issued a backgrounded `reboot` so the ack returned before disconnection, polled until node1 was reachable again, confirmed boot_id changed (446f0a24... -> ff186243...) with fresh uptime (~30s), and re-verified crond was running and the cron access control (wrapper file, directory permissions, allow/deny behavior for opsadmin vs alpine) was fully intact post-reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS and cron stack: Alpine 3.23 using busybox crond/crontab dispatched via /bin/bbsuid (setuid root, argv0-based applet dispatch)
Confirmed busybox crontab does not implement /etc/cron.allow or /etc/cron.deny
Created opsadmin user (adduser -D) and set a randomly generated password locally on the node via chpasswd
Created /usr/libexec/cron-real/crontab as a basename-preserving symlink to /bin/bbsuid, then locked the containing directory to root:cron mode 0710
Added opsadmin to the 'cron' group
Replaced /usr/bin/crontab with a wrapper script that allows only root/opsadmin to proceed and denies all other callers with an explicit error and exit 1
Enabled and started the crond service (rc-update add crond default; rc-service crond start)
Verified functionally: root and opsadmin can list/install/remove crontab entries; alpine user is denied via the wrapper and via direct invocation of the real crontab path
Captured pre-restart boot_id and service/data health baseline
Issued a backgrounded reboot on node1 so the exec ack returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec access returned
Confirmed boot_id changed post-restart, crond auto-started, and re-ran the root/opsadmin/alpine functional tests to confirm persistence of the access control after reboot

evidence.requirement: Baseline discovery: cron implementation is busybox with no native allow/deny, bbsuid dispatch confirmed
evidence.summary: Established node1 uses busybox crond/crontab via setuid /bin/bbsuid with basename-based applet dispatch, and that busybox crontab has no built-in cron.allow/cron.deny mechanism, motivating a wrapper-based access control design

evidence.requirement: opsadmin user created with generated credentials on the node
evidence.summary: Created opsadmin user (uid 1001) and set its password using a locally generated random string via chpasswd, without exposing the literal password

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs (mechanism implemented and enforced)
evidence.summary: Deployed the crontab wrapper enforcing root/opsadmin allowlist, locked down the real crontab binary's directory to root:cron 0710, and directly demonstrated: root works, opsadmin can list/install a crontab entry, alpine is denied both via the wrapper and via direct-path bypass attempt (Permission denied, exit 126)

evidence.requirement: crond service enabled/running so scheduling is functional
evidence.summary: Enabled crond at boot (rc-update add crond default) and started it; confirmed status started with running PID, and cleaned up the opsadmin test crontab entry

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot identity + service/data health)
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id (446f0a24-81fd-40b1-ace2-5570705ee7c1), confirmed crond running, root crontab intact, and wrapper/directory permissions intact

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnection, then node became unreachable
evidence.summary: Issued a backgrounded `reboot` on node1 whose scheduling command returned pid/ack immediately; subsequent exec calls failed with connection reset/timeout, proving the node went down

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed after restart, proving an actual reboot occurred
evidence.summary: Node1 became reachable again with /proc/uptime showing ~30s uptime, and /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id changed from 446f0a24-81fd-40b1-ace2-5570705ee7c1 to ff186243-c96c-4197-ac90-53b541c8ea04

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: cron service and access control persisted correctly
evidence.summary: After reboot, crond auto-started (enabled via rc-update), the wrapper script and locked-down real-crontab directory were unchanged, and functional re-test confirmed root/opsadmin can schedule cron jobs while the alpine user is still denied
